data.long_meaning: One who is dear to Lord Hari (Vishnu). In Hindu mythology, Hari is a name of God Vishnu, who is revered for protection and preservation. Harendar signifies the deep devotion and dedication towards the divine. The name Harendar carries the meaning “Lord Hari's beloved” and is chosen by families in Hindu traditions for the positive qualities it expresses. Linguistically it belongs to the Sanskrit tradition and is also used in Hindi, Sanskrit, Marathi. Parents who choose Harendar usually hope their child will grow to embody lord hari's beloved and live with faith, good character and purpose.

historical_references.reference: Harendar was a famous Hindu king of the Vijayanagara Empire in South India during the late 15th century.
historical_references.context: Harendar ruled over the Vijayanagara Empire at a time when it was facing numerous external threats, including invasions from the Deccan Sultanates. He is best remembered for leading a successful campaign against the Bahmani Sultanate, which helped to secure the empire's borders and preserve its power.

historical_references.reference: Another Harendar, a renowned Hindu saint and scholar, lived during the 14th century in Bengal, India.
historical_references.context: Harendar was a prominent figure in the Bhakti movement, which emphasized the importance of devotion to God through personal experience and emotion. He is believed to have composed numerous hymns and songs in praise of the goddess Kali, and his works continue to be revered by many Hindus in India and beyond.
